title: SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.26563v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agentic (tool-using) language models are mainly trained on tool-call traces and agent trajectories during post-training. These data provide direct behavioral supervision, but producing them requires task environments, execution, and verification, making broad tool and task coverage expensive. Publicly available skills offer another source of training data: they encode reusable tool semantics and workflows but are typically used only as inference-time context. We introduce Skill Pre-Training (SPT), a mid-training method that applies causal language modeling to SkillCorpus, a collection of public multi-file skill packages, optionally mixed with general data. To preserve relations among files within each package, we also introduce Reference Insert, a reference-aware assembly strategy that places supporting files near their mentions in the primary instruction. translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.26563v1 公告类型：新 摘要：智能体（工具使用）语言模型主要在后训练阶段基于工具调用轨迹和智能体行为序列进行训练。这些数据提供了直接的行为监督，但生成它们需要任务环境、执行和验证，这使得广泛覆盖工具和任务的成本高昂。公开可用的技能提供了另一种训练数据来源：它们编码了可复用的工具语义和工作流程，但通常仅作为推理时的上下文使用。我们引入了技能预训练（SPT），这是一种中间训练方法，将因果语言建模应用于SkillCorpus——一个包含公开多文件技能包的集合，可选地混合通用数据。为了保持每个包内文件之间的关系，我们还引入了引用插入（Reference Insert），这是一种引用感知的组装策略，将支持文件放置在主要指令中提及它们的位置附近。跨多个模型规模和后训练方案的实验表明，SPT能够...
tldr: 本文提出技能预训练（SPT）方法，通过将公开技能包作为中间训练数据，结合引用插入策略，显著提升智能体语言模型的工具使用能力。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Skill Pre-Training (SPT), which leverages public skill packages as mid-training data with a reference-aware assembly strategy, significantly enhancing agentic language models' tool-use capabilities.
